To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is a strong association between school hierarchy and violence, particularly intimidation; 2) popular students are more likely to be bullies and unpopular students are more likely victims; 3) popular students are less likely to be victims and unpopular students are less likely bullies; and 4) the more popular the student, the more likely he or she was a victim.

(a) the most popular, the best at physical education, and the worst academically were the most associated with perpetration of bullying and the least popular and worst at physical education were the most associated as victims of bullying, and (b) the least popular and the worst academies were the most associated victims of bullying and the most popular, and the best academies were the least associated with being bullied.
